Recommend **publish-verified-testimony**.

It best satisfies the Book 4 intent because **Monastery testimony: preserved** can re-enter public memory while **Archive protection: treaty protected** keeps the originals secure. That matters because the **Treaty: archive is the only evidentiary chain**. Verification also answers the political pressure created by **Council archive position: retracted admission**, while supporting the series commitment to conflict between official history and lived memory.

The principal tradeoff is delay. Authentication postpones public release, giving the council time to shape the public account. Even so, that cost is safer than **stage-protected-hearing**, which would expose the strongest archive records and put the only evidentiary chain at greater risk.

I deliberately excluded **Archive lantern condition: repaired** because it does not affect this choice. I also excluded the identity of the falsifier and the mechanics of the **Founding record: forged** because those facts establish the wider dispute but do not decide how testimony should be republished safely.

This is a non-authoritative recommendation. It creates no canon, Book Direction, or Canonical State.
